lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be omitted from the résumé.
items.because: They create unnecessary exposure to bias without supporting your qualifications.

items.says: Education appears ahead of the stronger professional and product trajectory.
items.because: Recruiters should encounter the professional experience and relevant product internship before academic credentials.

items.says: The timeline has an unexplained eight-month gap between the B.A. and the Operations Analyst role.
“By 35%” does not clarify whether the gain was relative or in percentage points, or give a measurement window.
items.because: The interpretations represent materially different gains, and the comparison period is needed to judge the figure.

items.says: Shipping two weeks ahead of plan shows delivery performance but not the feature’s post-launch value.
items.because: Without an adoption, resolution-time or support-demand outcome, the line shows delivery more clearly than product impact.

items.says: The $1.1 million finding and roadmap effect are buried behind the research methods.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the strongest evidence late.

items.says: “1.1 million dollars” is less scannable than standard résumé notation.
“Over the summer” repeats the internship dates in the heading.
The opt-in comparison cannot validly measure the redesign’s causal effect as written.
items.because: Merchants who chose the new flow may differ systematically from those who stayed on the old flow.

items.says: The comparison method is given without the outcome it found.
items.because: A study design alone does not show whether the flow performed better or informed a decision.

items.says: The opt-in comparison does not support the separate claim of A/B-testing experience.
items.because: An A/B test randomly assigns participants, whereas these merchants chose whether to opt in.

items.says: The same onboarding result across 2,300 merchants is attributed to both this internship and the hospital practicum.
items.because: The unrelated practicum ended before the internship began and otherwise concerns clinics and patient intake.

items.says: “Cut late deliveries” is false because excluding weather-delayed shipments changes only the reported calculation.
items.because: It does not change whether any shipment arrived late.

items.says: The business purpose of the revised late-delivery measure is unstated.
items.because: The line does not say what planning, accountability or service decision it enabled.

items.says: “30%” does not specify whether the reduction was relative or when it was measured.
items.because: Without those anchors, a reader cannot interpret its exact size or durability.

items.says: “Two sites” is inconsistent with the entry’s numeral formatting.
“Prepares” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in August 2023.
items.because: It describes an ongoing responsibility and conflicts with “Coordinated” in the same sentence.

items.says: The S&OP activities have no stated business result.
items.because: The line reads as a responsibility rather than showing a decision or improvement the work enabled.

items.says: “Prepares the forecast pack” does not reveal the analytical work personally performed.
items.because: It could mean document assembly or substantive forecasting, which imply different levels of skill.

items.says: “S&OP” is not expanded for readers outside the function.
“Led the rollout” does not clarify the substantive configuration or analytical contribution.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the work involved routing logic, constraints or data, or mainly deployment coordination.

items.says: The route-planning result is the entry’s strongest bullet but appears last.
items.because: Its scale and time savings would give a scanning recruiter a stronger first impression.

items.says: “To 3,100 students” does not distinguish users from students merely eligible for access.
items.because: Registrations, active users and an addressable audience indicate different levels of adoption.

items.says: “Launched a surplus-food pickup app” does not show the product or launch decision personally driven.
items.because: A concrete decision or mechanism would make product-lead ownership visible.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” is unnecessarily wordy.
“Its” has an unclear referent.
“Volunteer shift system” does not explain what changed in scheduling or coverage management.
items.because: A specific mechanism would connect the action to the coverage improvement.

items.says: “Each week” and “a week” repeat the same timeframe.
“Staff cover shifts” is unclear to readers outside the operation.
The line gives no decision, recommendation, implementation or scheduling improvement.
items.because: Meeting cadence alone does not establish that the consulting work produced value.

items.says: “Held weekly working sessions” weakly and vaguely describes the contribution.
items.because: It does not show whether you directed the sessions or what diagnostic work occurred.

items.says: The passive construction hides ownership of the intake work.
items.because: It makes the process the grammatical actor and weakens the action-to-result flow.

items.says: “The intake form was shortened” has no before-and-after measure.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the redesign was minor or substantial.

items.says: Front-desk adoption does not state what the changes improved.
items.because: Adoption shows implementation but not a patient or operational benefit.

items.says: The line does not explain how the intake problems or unnecessary fields were found.
The strongest hospital-related bullet is not placed first.
The merchant-onboarding bullet is assigned to the wrong entry.
items.because: Merchants and first payments do not fit the hospital engagement, and the achievement also appears under Harbor Payments.

items.says: “Halved the time” is mathematically inconsistent with a reduction from 9 days to 4.
items.because: Half of 9 is 4.5; the stated reduction is approximately 56%.

items.says: “By redesigning onboarding” is too broad to show what changed.
items.because: Without the specific intervention, a reader cannot connect the work to the time reduction.

items.says: The result wording is wordy and the cohort placement interrupts it.
items.because: “The time it takes” delays the metric, while the commas slow scanning of the result and method.
